gen-archivo-fs-karma: Editorial and sure of itself, Archivo leads with light-passing exits. Karma, a serif, keeps its terminals well away from the stem, and its modulation is gentle enough that nothing snags the eye.
gen-audiowide-fs-karma: Audiowide spaces its glyphs like tiles with wide grout lines, futuristic and tall in the lowercase, with no stroke shift at all. Karma adds a trustworthy, classic body whose modulation never snags the eye.
gen-audiowide-gf-cossette-titre: Cossette Titre keeps its bowls open and its capitals barely taller than the lowercase. Cossette Titre sits beneath Audiowide, whose outline-like skeleton keeps one fixed stroke thickness and a futuristic feel.
gen-audiowide-gf-noto-sans-old-persian: Marker-drawn plainness with a futuristic edge, that's Audiowide all over. Noto Sans Old Persian has open counters and a lofty lowercase, so text running on for pages breathes easily.
gen-audiowide-gf-noto-serif-grantha: Audiowide cuts its futuristic letters like laser-cut sheet, one cutting width throughout, with tall lowercase and no stroke shift. Noto Serif Grantha, a text serif, reads smoothly with its moderate contrast.
gen-audiowide-gf-roboto-condensed: Futuristic tiles set with wide grout lines: that's Audiowide. Roboto Condensed, a sans, packs its enlarged lowercase tight, words nearly touching, a line gliding under the eye like wire.
gen-audiowide-outfit: Futuristic and tall in the lowercase, Audiowide has no stroke shift between its downstrokes and curves. And Outfit bends open-ended curves like cable, which keeps paragraphs feeling clean and approachable.
gen-bebas-neue-fs-erode: Thick, clustered, contrast-free: Bebas Neue is a solid band of letters. Erode brings a tall middle band, broad apertures and a faint nib-pressure ebb that makes the heading's blunt sameness feel dignified.
gen-bebas-neue-fs-hoover: Ballpoint-pen stroke widths, no contrast, trimmed ascenders: that's Bebas Neue. Bebas Neue shouts in a tight cluster, while Hoover, a serif with compressed ascenders and a generous e, is good for a couple of lines.
gen-bebas-neue-fs-literata: Blunt, tightly packed capitals with zero stroke contrast, that's Bebas Neue. It earns its keep big and short, while Literata, a serif with sturdy thin lines and open-mouthed curves, handles the sophisticated, bookish side.
